intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is a must for thrill-seekers, offering breathtaking views of the Central Otago landscape before the ultimate freefall lasting approximately 8.5 seconds.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular Great Walks, a 32km trail through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Trek through ancient beech forests, alpine meadows, and past stunning glacial lakes with panoramic views of the Southern Alps. A multi-day hike best done over 2-3 days.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Equivalent: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Hike the challenging Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a 10km round trip gaining 1000m in elevation. Reward yourself with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Glacier, and turquoise glacial lakes. Overnight stays in the DOC hut are available for a truly immersive alpine experience.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy jump site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River in a scenic gorge setting. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is perfect for first-timers and includes the option to touch the water on your jump.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayaking adventure on the mirror-like waters of Milford Sound with a hike along the Milford foreshore track. Paddle beneath towering 1200-meter cliffs, spot fur seals and dolphins, and witness the majestic Stirling and Bowen Falls up close. A truly unforgettable Fiordland wilderness experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Equivalent: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Hike the challenging Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a 10km round trip gaining 1000m in elevation. Reward yourself with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Glacier, and turquoise glacial lakes. Overnight stays in the DOC hut are available for a truly immersive alpine experience.

day_by_day.morning: N/A — Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$4 NZD) from the airport into Queenstown town centre. Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Drop bags, freshen up, and take a short orientation walk along the Queenstown waterfront and Lake Wakatipu foreshore — completely free and stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's lively town centre on foot. Browse the weekend markets if still running. Head to Fergburger (iconic budget-friendly spot) for an early dinner to beat the queues.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport on arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap bite at the airport or a supermarket sandwich in town (~$5–8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Fergburger, Queenstown — massive, filling burgers from ~$15 NZD. Cash-friendly and legendary among budget travellers.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and orientation. No strenuous activity — rest and acclimatise. Pick up a free Queenstown map from the i-SITE visitor centre near the waterfront. Buy a local SIM card at the airport (Skinny or 2degrees are cheapest). Confirm your bungee and hike bookings for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast, then head to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (free, ~2–3 hours, 4km return). Start from Belfast Terrace. The trail winds through pine forest to a 907m summit with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. A perfect warm-up hike to gauge fitness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to Frankton Arm Walkway along the lake shore (free, flat, ~5km one way). Walk or cycle sections of it. Alternatively, visit the Queenstown Gardens (free entry) — rose gardens, disc golf, and lakeside lawns. Stop at New World Supermarket on Gorge Road to stock up on budget groceries for picnic lunches throughout the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using supermarket supplies to save money. Alternatively, visit Vudu Cafe & Larder for affordable shared plates or try the Queenstown Night Market (runs Thursdays — note for later in the week).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation (~$2–3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed supermarket lunch eaten at Queenstown Gardens lakeside (~$5–7 NZD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or stir-fry at accommodation (~$6–8 NZD) OR Vudu Cafe (~$18–22 NZD for a meal)

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Hill is free and underrated — far fewer crowds than Ben Lomond. Wear layers; summit can be cool even in November. This day is intentionally moderate to help with jet lag recovery before bigger adventures begin.

day_by_day.morning: Big adventure day — Nevis Bungy Jump! Book in advance through AJ Hackett (Nevis Bungy, 134m, the highest in New Zealand, ~$275 NZD). The Nevis Valley is accessed via AJ Hackett's dedicated shuttle from Queenstown (~$35 NZD return, often bundled). Depart early at ~8:30am. The jump pod hangs over the Nevis River gorge — an absolutely unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Adrenaline still pumping — celebrate with a walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront. Browse the free gondola base area. If budget allows, consider the Skyline Gondola (~$35 NZD) for views, though the luge adds cost — optional.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a well-earned dinner out. Head to The Cow Restaurant (pizza and pasta in a rustic stone cottage, ~$20–25 NZD per person) — one of Queenstown's best value sit-down restaurants. Book ahead as it fills quickly.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at accommodation before shuttle (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat after the jump — sandwiches and snacks from supermarket (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant, Queenstown — wood-fired pizza from ~$22 NZD. BYO wine option available to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy is a significant budget spend but is a once-in-a-lifetime experience and the headline adventure of the trip. Book at least 2–3 days in advance online for best pricing. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. No loose jewellery. GoPro hire available on-site (~$50 NZD) — optional but worth it for memories. The shuttle departs from the AJ Hackett base on Shotover Street.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the Nevis jump. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast. Then take the free Queenstown to Arrowtown Heritage Trail drive (~28km, ~35 min). Arrowtown is a beautifully preserved 1860s gold-rush town. Walk the free Chinese Settlement archaeological site and stroll the main street of heritage buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Arrow River Bridges Trail (free, ~4.5km, easy–moderate, 1.5 hours). The trail follows the Arrow River through a dramatic schist gorge with suspension bridges. Alternatively, pan for gold in the Arrow River — rent a pan locally for ~$5 NZD and try your luck. Visit the Lakes District Museum in Arrowtown (~$10 NZD entry) for gold rush history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for the Thursday Night Market (note: this is Wednesday — adjust if needed, or visit the Earnslaw Wharf area). Self-cater dinner or grab cheap takeaways from Queenstown's food court area near the Mall.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — eggs on toast (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch by the Arrow River — supermarket supplies (~$6 NZD). Dorothy Browns boutique cinema café in Arrowtown also offers affordable snacks.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation (~$7 NZD) OR cheap kebab/Thai takeaway in Queenstown town centre (~$12–15 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is a free or very low-cost day and a genuine highlight of the Queenstown region. The autumn leaves are gone by November but the schist rock scenery is beautiful year-round. Drive carefully on Crown Range Road if taking the scenic route back — it is steep and winding but spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take InterCity bus toward Wanaka (~1 hour from Queenstown via Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in NZ, free and scenic). Arrive in Wanaka by mid-morning. Walk to the famous Wanaka Tree (lone willow in the lake) — free and iconic. Stroll the Wanaka lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop (free, ~4.5km, ~2.5 hours, moderate). Trailhead is ~20 min drive from Wanaka town. Stunning elevated views over Lake Wanaka and the Southern Alps. Diamond Lake itself is a beautiful turquoise tarn. This is one of the best free hikes in the Wanaka area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka town. Visit Pemberton's Ice Cream for a cheap treat (~$5 NZD). Head back toward Queenstown or stay overnight in Wanaka (budget hostel ~$35–45 NZD/night at Wanaka Bakpaka if preferred). Thursday is Queenstown Night Market night — if returning, don't miss it on Earnslaw Wharf (cheap street food, ~$8–15 NZD per dish).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Diamond Lake after the hike — packed supermarket food (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market (Thursdays, Earnslaw Wharf) — various stalls, budget-friendly, ~$10–15 NZD for a full meal OR self-cater at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Crown Range Road offers some of the most dramatic scenery in the South Island — stop at the summit viewpoint. Diamond Lake trail can be muddy after rain — wear hiking boots. If staying in Wanaka overnight, this opens up more Wanaka hiking time on Day 6. Check road conditions on the NZTA Journey Planner app.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown toward Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (~3.5 hours via SH8 through the Mackenzie Basin). Depart by 7:30am. Stop at Lake Pukaki viewpoint — the impossibly turquoise glacier-fed lake with Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in it is one of New Zealand's most iconic views. Completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mount Cook Village (~12:30pm). Check in to YHA Aoraki Mount Cook (budget dorm ~$45–55 NZD/night — book well in advance). After dropping bags, do the Kea Point Track (free, 2km return, ~1 hour, easy) for close-up views of the Mueller Glacier and terminal lake. Outstanding and accessible for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the Hooker Valley Track start for a sunset preview walk (or do the first section). The alpenglow on Aoraki at dusk is extraordinary. Cook dinner at YHA's well-equipped kitchen — self-catering is essential here as the only restaurant (Old Mountaineers Café) is expensive (~$25–35 NZD mains).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at Queenstown accommodation before departure (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Pukaki viewpoint (~$6 NZD) — there are picnic tables at the lake edge
meals.dinner: Self-catered at YHA kitchen (~$8–10 NZD) — pasta, canned tomatoes, vegetables. Buy supplies in Twizel (~30 min before Mount Cook) as there is no supermarket at the village.

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Stock up on ALL food supplies in Twizel (New World supermarket) before reaching Mount Cook Village. There is no supermarket at the village and the café is very expensive. Fill your petrol tank in Twizel as well. Book YHA well in advance — it fills up fast in November (peak season). Bring warm layers even in November — altitude and wind chill can be significant.

day_by_day.morning: THE HIGHLIGHT DAY — Mueller Hut Route. Start early at 7:00am from the White Horse Hill Campground trailhead (5 min walk from YHA). The Mueller Hut Route is 10km return with ~1,030m elevation gain. The first section follows the Kea Point Track before ascending steeply via 2,200 steps cut into the ridge. Mueller Hut sits at 1,800m with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Mueller Glacier, and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Mueller Hut by late morning (~3–4 hours up). Spend time at the hut enjoying the views, eating lunch, and resting. The hut itself is a New Zealand Alpine Club facility (~$45 NZD/night if staying, or free to visit during the day). Begin descent by 1:00–2:00pm to allow plenty of daylight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to White Horse Hill by late afternoon (~5:00–6:00pm). Tired but exhilarated. Hot shower at YHA. Cook a hearty self-catered dinner at YHA kitchen. Stargaze from the village — Mount Cook is in an International Dark Sky Reserve, one of the best stargazing locations in the Southern Hemisphere.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at YHA — porridge and coffee at 6:30am (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed high-energy trail lunch eaten at Mueller Hut — sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, fruit (~$8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty meal at YHA — rice, lentils, vegetables (~$8–10 NZD). You deserve a big meal tonight.

day_by_day.notes: Mueller Hut Route is rated DIFFICULT. Do NOT attempt in bad weather — check the MetService mountain forecast the night before. Carry: 2L+ water (refillable at hut), snacks, sunscreen, sunglasses, warm layers, waterproof jacket, first aid kit. Poles are recommended for the steep descent. Start as early as possible to avoid afternoon cloud build-up common in summer. This is the equivalent of the Tongariro Alpine Crossing experience on the South Island — a genuinely world-class alpine hike.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after Mueller Hut. Do the Hooker Valley Track (free, 10km return, ~3 hours, easy) — one of New Zealand's most beautiful flat walks, crossing three swing bridges to Hooker Lake at the foot of Aoraki/Mount Cook. The views are extraordinary and the walk is completely flat — perfect for tired legs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown (~3.5 hours) via the Mackenzie Basin. Stop at Lake Tekapo on the way (~1 hour from Mount Cook). Visit the Church of the Good Shepherd (free entry, iconic lakeside stone church) and walk the lakefront. Lake Tekapo township has affordable cafés for a late lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Queenstown by early evening. Unpack, do laundry at accommodation. Quiet self-catered dinner. Plan remaining Queenstown days.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at YHA before checkout (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Café in Lake Tekapo — try Kohan Japanese Restaurant for surprisingly affordable lunch sets (~$15–18 NZD) or grab a pie from a bakery (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Queenstown accommodation (~$7–8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Hooker Valley Track is unmissable — do not skip it even with tired legs. It is completely flat and the views rival anything on the Mueller Hut Route. Check out of YHA by 10:00am. If time permits, the Tekapo Springs area has free access to the outdoor hot pools area for a quick soak (~$25 NZD if using the hot pools — optional treat).

day_by_day.morning: Ben Lomond Track — the big Queenstown hike. Start early from the Queenstown Gondola base (walk up the zigzag trail for free rather than paying for the gondola). The full Ben Lomond Track is ~11km return from the gondola, gaining ~1,450m to the 1,748m summit. Allow 5–7 hours total. Alternatively, hike to the Saddle only (~2 hours from gondola) for great views if energy is lower after Mueller Hut.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and reward yourself. If you took the gondola down (~$35 NZD — optional), enjoy the views. Walk back to town along the Tiki Trail (free). Visit the Queenstown Memorial Centre or simply relax by the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Night Market is on Thursdays — tonight is Monday so self-cater or try Winnies Pizza on the Mall (affordable pizza slices ~$6–8 NZD each). Sit by the lake as the sun sets over The Remarkables.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at 6:30am (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten on Ben Lomond summit or saddle (~$7 NZD) — views from the top are among the best in the South Island
meals.dinner: Winnies Pizza, Queenstown (~$15–20 NZD) OR self-catered at accommodation (~$7 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a serious hike — only attempt if legs have recovered from Mueller Hut. The Saddle is a worthy alternative if the full summit feels too much. Carry plenty of water — the summit section is exposed and can be very hot in November. Start no later than 8:00am. The Tiki Trail from the gondola base is free and well-signposted.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (~45 min from Queenstown, free, stunning lakeside road). This small village at the head of Lake Wakatipu is the gateway to some of New Zealand's most remote wilderness. Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (free, ~1 hour, flat) through wetlands and native bush with views of snow-capped peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Paradise area (4WD track, ~20 min from Glenorchy) — filming location for Lord of the Rings. Walk the Paradise Track (free, ~2 hours return, easy–moderate) through beech forest and open river flats. The scenery is otherworldly. Return to Queenstown by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening. Visit the Queenstown waterfront at sunset. Try Taco Medic for budget-friendly tacos (~$6–8 NZD each) — a Queenstown institution with great value.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at Paradise — eat by the Dart River flats (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: Taco Medic, Queenstown (~$15–18 NZD for 2–3 tacos) OR self-catered (~$7 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Glenorchy is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand — stop at multiple viewpoints. The road to Paradise requires a high-clearance vehicle for the final section — check conditions. Glenorchy has a small café (The Glenorchy Café) for affordable coffee and snacks. Fill petrol in Queenstown before going — no petrol station in Glenorchy.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Fiordland — depart Queenstown by 8:00am for Te Anau (~2 hours). Te Anau is the gateway to Milford Sound/Piopiotahi. Stop at the Te Anau Glowworm Caves if budget allows (~$55 NZD — optional). Otherwise, walk the free Te Anau Lakefront Track (~3km, 1 hour, flat, beautiful views across the lake to Fiordland mountains).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the Milford Road (SH94) from Te Anau toward Milford Sound (~2 hours, one of the world's great scenic drives). Stop at Mirror Lakes (free, 5 min walk, stunning reflections), The Chasm (free, 15 min walk, dramatic waterfall gorge), and Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget Milford Sound cruise — Real Journeys or Jucy Cruize offer cruises from ~$55–75 NZD. The evening cruise often has fewer crowds and beautiful light. See Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls. Return to Te Anau for the night — budget accommodation at Te Anau YHA or Barnyard Backpackers (~$35–45 NZD/night dorm).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at Queenstown before departure (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirror Lakes or The Chasm (~$6 NZD) — there are no budget food options on the Milford Road
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel kitchen (~$8 NZD) OR The Sandfly Café, Te Anau (~$15–20 NZD for a meal)

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: There is NO food available between Te Anau and Milford Sound — pack all food for the day before leaving. The Milford Road is one of the world's great scenic drives but can close due to avalanche or weather — check NZTA alerts before departure. Book your Milford cruise well in advance. Jucy Cruize is typically the most budget-friendly option. The drive back from Milford to Te Anau in the evening light is magical.

day_by_day.morning: Morning in Te Anau. Walk the Te Anau Bird Sanctuary (free entry) — see the rare takahē, a flightless bird once thought extinct. Stroll the Te Anau waterfront. Have a coffee at a local café before departing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Queenstown (~2 hours). Stop at Kingston at the southern end of Lake Wakatipu for views and a quick walk. Arrive in Queenstown by early afternoon. Last chance for any souvenir shopping (try the Saturday markets or op-shops for budget finds). Visit the Queenstown i-SITE to return any rental equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Queenstown — it's Thursday, so the Queenstown Night Market is on at Earnslaw Wharf! Enjoy the best of the market's street food from multiple stalls (~$10–15 NZD for a full meal). Walk the waterfront one last time. Sunset drinks at a lakeside spot (buy a beer from a supermarket and sit by the lake — free and perfect).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or pie from a bakery in Te Anau before departure (~$5–8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Thursday Night Market, Earnslaw Wharf (~$12–15 NZD) — the best budget dining experience in Queenstown. Try multiple stalls.

day_by_day.notes: If time allows on the drive back, detour to the Mavora Lakes (~1 hour off SH94) — a stunning remote lake system used as a Lord of the Rings filming location (Nen Hithoel). Requires ~1 hour extra and a gravel road but is completely free and extraordinarily beautiful. Only attempt in a suitable vehicle.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Depending on departure time, do one last easy walk — the Queenstown Botanic Gardens (free) or the short Queenstown Hill lower trail section. Pack bags and check out of accommodation. Grab a farewell flat white from a local café — try Vudu Café or Bespoke Kitchen for quality coffee at reasonable prices (~$5–6 NZD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Queenstown Airport for departure. Allow extra time for check-in. Browse the airport shops — Countdown supermarket near the airport is a last chance for cheap snacks. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the South Island.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry snacks from the supermarket to avoid expensive airport food.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at accommodation or café coffee and muffin (~$8–10 NZD as a treat)
meals.lunch: Supermarket snacks or a final Fergburger if time allows (~$15 NZD)
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport food if departure is evening

day_by_day.notes: BUDGET SUMMARY ESTIMATE (NZD per person): Accommodation ~$500–600 (mix of hostel dorms and boutique stay), Transport ~$150–200 (bus, fuel share, shuttles), Nevis Bungy ~$275–310, Milford Sound Cruise ~$55–75, Mueller Hut day hike ~free, Food ~$350–420 (heavy self-catering), Activities/entrance fees ~$50–100. TOTAL ESTIMATE: ~$1,380–1,705 NZD for 13 days excluding flights. TOP BUDGET TIPS: (1) Self-cater all breakfasts and lunches. (2) Buy all Mount Cook food in Twizel. (3) Use Orbus public buses in Queenstown. (4) All major hikes are free. (5) Thursday Night Market is the best value dining in Queenstown.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport, clear customs and collect luggage. Transfer to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay (~30-40 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the Queenstown lakefront and town centre to get your bearings and soak in the stunning Remarkables mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Queenstown Bay waterfront and browse the lively town centre. Head to dinner at a local restaurant to kick off the trip.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport café upon arrival — try a flat white and a pie, a classic Kiwi combo (~NZD 15-20)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — mid-range New Zealand cuisine featuring local lamb and seasonal produce (~NZD 45-65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag may be a factor. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings (Nevis Bungy, Routeburn, Kawarau) at the i-SITE visitor centre in town. Pick up a Queenstown area map and check the weather forecast for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump (~20 min drive from Queenstown). Arrive early for your 9:00am session at the world's first commercial bungy site — a 43m plunge above the turquoise Kawarau River. Watch other jumpers, browse the on-site museum about bungy history, and collect your certificate and video package.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, drive the scenic Gibbston Valley wine road back toward Queenstown. Stop at Gibbston Valley Winery for a cave wine tasting and cellar door lunch — the region is famous for its Pinot Noir. Return to the hotel for a relaxing afternoon swim or spa if available.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant Steamer Wharf precinct. Enjoy sunset views over Lake Wakatipu before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby Vudu Café & Larder — excellent eggs and locally roasted coffee (~NZD 18-25)
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery cellar door — cheese platters, charcuterie boards paired with a Pinot Noir tasting (~NZD 30-40)
meals.dinner: Fergburger on Shotover Street — legendary Queenstown institution, massive gourmet burgers (~NZD 18-22). Arrive early or expect a queue!

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bungy in advance online through AJ Hackett. Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes. The jump video package is worth purchasing (~NZD 40 extra) for memories. Gibbston Valley is en route back so no extra driving needed.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day preparation and travel day for the Routeburn Track Great Walk. Drive from Queenstown to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (~1.5 hours). Begin hiking from the Routeburn Flat end. Morning section covers Routeburn Flats — a gentle walk through beech forest with stunning valley views and the Routeburn River alongside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking to Routeburn Falls Hut (1,000m elevation). The afternoon section climbs steadily through subalpine terrain with cascading waterfalls. Arrive at the hut by mid-afternoon, check in, dry gear, and enjoy panoramic views of the Harris Mountains. Socialize with fellow trampers.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from Routeburn Falls Hut deck — one of the finest views on the entire track. Prepare your own dinner using hut kitchen facilities or enjoy your packed supplies.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure, or pack muesli bars and fruit for the road
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared the night before — sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars, and a thermos of tea/coffee eaten at Routeburn Flats
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the DOC hut — bring a freeze-dried meal or pack pasta and sauce. Huts have gas cookers and basic utensils

day_by_day.notes: Book DOC Great Walks hut passes well in advance (opens May each year — extremely popular). Pack rain gear regardless of forecast — Fiordland weather is unpredictable. Carry 2L of water, blister plasters, and layers. Distance today: ~11km, elevation gain: ~490m. Difficulty: moderate.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Routeburn Falls Hut. The morning section is the most spectacular — climb above the bushline to Harris Saddle (1,255m) with 360-degree views across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains. On a clear day, you can see all the way to Milford Sound. Optional side trip to Conical Hill summit adds 45 min but is absolutely worth it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle through the Hollyford Valley side of the track, passing Lake Harris and through ancient beech forest to Lake Mackenzie Hut. Arrive by early afternoon, rest, and take a dip in the crystal-clear lake if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Lake Mackenzie Hut, one of the most scenic hut locations in New Zealand. Watch alpenglow on the mountains at dusk. Share stories with fellow hikers.

meals.breakfast: Hot oats or instant porridge cooked at the hut — fuel up for the big climb ahead
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Harris Saddle — this is the highlight viewpoint, so linger and enjoy. Trail mix, crackers with cheese, chocolate
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Lake Mackenzie Hut — freeze-dried meal or pre-packed dinner. Treat yourself to some chocolate for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Today is the hardest and most rewarding day of the Routeburn Track. Distance: ~11km, elevation gain/loss: significant. Weather at Harris Saddle can change rapidly — have full waterproofs accessible at the top of your pack. The views from Conical Hill on a clear November day are extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Final section of the Routeburn Track. Depart Lake Mackenzie Hut early and hike the remaining ~10km to The Divide on the Milford Road. The trail descends through stunning Fiordland rainforest with hanging valleys and waterfalls. Reach The Divide by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the pre-arranged shuttle bus from The Divide to Te Anau (~1 hour), then connect to Queenstown (~2.5 hours). Arrive back at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay by late afternoon. Hot shower — the best shower of your life after 3 days on the track! Rest and do laundry.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Routeburn Track with a proper sit-down dinner in Queenstown. Enjoy a well-earned glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Lake Mackenzie Hut before departing
meals.lunch: Pack a final trail lunch for the last hiking section — eat at The Divide before the shuttle
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant, Queenstown — cozy, intimate bistro-style dining with excellent NZ beef and venison (~NZD 45-60 per person). Treat yourself!

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Tracknet shuttle from The Divide to Te Anau and onward connection to Queenstown. Alternatively, book a private transfer. Check shuttle times when booking hut passes. Total Routeburn Track distance completed over 3 days: ~32km. Well done!

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and let your legs recover. Gentle stroll along the Queenstown Gardens peninsula — flat, easy walking with beautiful lake views and rose gardens. Visit the free Queenstown Arts Centre if open.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables. Try the luge track (2-3 runs) for some light-hearted fun. Browse the summit observation deck and visit the Maori cultural experience at the top.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Skyline restaurant bar before descending, or walk back down the Tiki Trail (45 min, easy descent through pine forest). Dinner in Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Vudu Café & Larder — full cooked breakfast with eggs your way, avocado toast, and excellent coffee (~NZD 22-28)
meals.lunch: Skyline Gondola summit café — buffet lunch with views (~NZD 35-45 per person, included in some gondola packages)
meals.dinner: Pub lunch style at The Pub on Wharf — craft beers on tap, fish and chips, and relaxed lakeside atmosphere (~NZD 25-35)

day_by_day.notes: The Skyline Gondola costs approximately NZD 32 return for adults. Luge runs are extra (~NZD 12 per run). The Tiki Trail walk down is free and a lovely way to end the afternoon. This is a genuine recovery day — don't over-plan it.

day_by_day.morning: The crown jewel of the trip — Nevis Bungy Jump! Transfer to the Nevis Valley jump site (~45 min from Queenstown by AJ Hackett shuttle). At 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge, this is New Zealand's highest bungy jump. Arrive early for briefing, harness fitting, and the nerve-wracking cable car ride to the suspended pod. Take the leap!
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown on the shuttle, buzzing with adrenaline. Visit the AJ Hackett base on Shotover Street to collect your certificate and watch your video. Afternoon free — consider a jet boat ride on the Shotover River (~1.5 hours) to keep the adrenaline flowing, or relax by the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the Nevis jump milestone with a special dinner. This is a highlight evening of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the jump — don't eat too heavily! Toast, banana, and water at the hotel
meals.lunch: Post-jump celebration lunch at Amisfield Bistro, Queenstown — excellent Central Otago wine and seasonal menu (~NZD 40-55)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant (revisit) or try Botswana Butchery on Marine Parade — premium NZ beef and lamb with lake views (~NZD 50-70)

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy costs approximately NZD 275 per person. Book weeks in advance — it sells out, especially on weekends. Weight limits apply (45-127kg). The shuttle from Queenstown is included in the price. Video and photo package strongly recommended (~NZD 50 extra). This is a bucket-list moment!

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (~45 min from Queenstown along the stunning Lake Wakatipu shore road — one of the most scenic drives in NZ). Explore the small town and walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hours, flat and easy). The Humboldt Mountains and Paradise valley backdrop is jaw-dropping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Paradise (the filming location for Lothlórien in Lord of the Rings) for a short forest walk. Return via the Kinloch Road loop if conditions permit. Stop at a picnic spot for lunch with mountain views. Drive back to Queenstown via the lake road.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Browse the night markets if it's Sunday (Queenstown Night Market runs Sunday evenings on the waterfront).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before the scenic drive
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed at Paradise or Glenorchy Lagoon — grab supplies from New World supermarket the evening before
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market (Sunday only) — try various food stalls: NZ green-lipped mussels, venison burgers, crepes, and local desserts (~NZD 20-30 for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown to Glenorchy road (State Highway 6) is one of the most photographed drives in the South Island — stop at multiple pull-offs for photos. The road to Paradise requires a standard 2WD vehicle in dry conditions. Check conditions locally. Glenorchy has a small café and basic facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (~3.5 hours via State Highway 8 through the Mackenzie Basin). The drive itself is spectacular — passing Lake Pukaki with its impossibly turquoise glacier-fed water and the first views of Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724m, New Zealand's highest peak). Arrive by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Mueller Hut Route — one of the most rewarding day hikes in New Zealand. Start from the Aoraki/Mount Cook Village and ascend via the Sealy Tarns Track (steep boardwalk stairs) to the Mueller Hut at 1,800m. The 10km round trip gains 1,000m elevation. If doing as a day hike, aim to reach the hut and return before dark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mount Cook Village by late afternoon/early evening. Check in at accommodation in the village area. Dinner with views of the Southern Alps.

meals.breakfast: Roadside stop at Tekapo for breakfast — Mackenzie's Bar & Grill or a café on the main street (~NZD 18-25). Enjoy views of Lake Tekapo and the Church of the Good Shepherd
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mueller Hut or Sealy Tarns — the views make any food taste extraordinary
meals.dinner: Old Mountaineers Café & Bar at Mount Cook Village — hearty NZ meals, great atmosphere, local craft beer (~NZD 30-45)

day_by_day.notes: Mueller Hut Route difficulty: HARD. Requires good fitness, sturdy hiking boots, and full weather gear. November conditions can include snow at higher elevations — check with DOC visitor centre upon arrival. The Sealy Tarns boardwalk has 2,200 steps. Start no later than 10am for a day hike. Alternatively, book Mueller Hut for an overnight stay for a sunrise experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk to the Hooker Valley Track (3-4 hours return, easy-moderate) — arguably the most accessible and stunning valley walk in the park. Three swing bridges, glacier lake views, icebergs floating in Hooker Lake, and Aoraki/Mount Cook directly ahead. Best done in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Mount Cook to Te Anau (~3.5 hours via State Highway 8 and 94), the gateway to Fiordland National Park. This is a long but scenic drive through the Mackenzie Basin, Burkes Pass, and into Southland. Check in at Te Anau accommodation. Short walk around Lake Te Anau foreshore to stretch legs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Te Anau town — small but charming. Visit the DOC visitor centre to confirm Milford Sound plans for the following day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Old Mountaineers Café before the Hooker Valley walk opens — or pack breakfast bars for the trail
meals.lunch: Picnic at Hooker Lake terminal face — pack supplies from the Mount Cook Village store
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — excellent Fiordland cuisine featuring venison, salmon, and local produce in a cozy atmosphere (~NZD 40-55)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is one of the most rewarding easy walks in New Zealand — do not skip it. Icebergs in Hooker Lake are a feature of November. The drive to Te Anau is long — depart Mount Cook by 1:00pm at the latest. Fuel up in Twizel as petrol stations are sparse on this route.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo. Depart Te Anau at 7:00am for the spectacular Milford Road drive (~2 hours) — one of the world's great scenic drives passing Homer Tunnel, Mirror Lakes, and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain. Arrive at Milford Sound and meet your guided kayak and hike group.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sea kayak on the mirror-like waters of Milford Sound, paddling beneath Mitre Peak (1,692m) and past Stirling Falls and Lady Bowen Falls. Seals, dolphins, and penguins are commonly spotted. After kayaking, join the hike component along a section of the Milford Track or a local nature trail through Fiordland rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau (arrive ~7:00pm). Tired but euphoric — Milford Sound is one of the world's great natural wonders. Casual dinner in Te Anau.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before 7:00am departure — cereal, toast, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the kayak tour operator, or bring your own — eaten on the water or at a rest stop
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies or The Fat Duck, Te Anau — relaxed, affordable dinner after a big day (~NZD 20-35)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo well in advance — this is a premium experience (~NZD 200-250 per person). Wear warm, quick-dry layers under the provided kayak gear even in November — the water is cold. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a waterproof camera or dry bag for your phone. Milford Sound receives 8 meters of rain annually — embrace the mist!

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau and drive back to Queenstown (~2.5 hours). Stop at Kingston on the southern tip of Lake Wakatipu for photos. Arrive in Queenstown by mid-morning. Check back in at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Use the morning to repack, do any final laundry, and organize gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Queenstown — treat yourself to a relaxing Shotover River jet boat experience if not done earlier (45 min, ~NZD 149), or take the easy Queenstown Hill Time Walk (3 hours return, moderate) for panoramic farewell views of the entire region — Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, Cecil Peak, and Walter Peak.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Queenstown. Splurge slightly on a memorable final evening meal. Browse Queenstown's boutique shops for last-minute New Zealand souvenirs — Manuka honey, Merino wool, and pounamu (greenstone) jewellery.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Queenstown's Vudu Café or a food truck on the waterfront (~NZD 18-25)
meals.dinner: Amisfield Bistro on Lake Hayes (~20 min from Queenstown) — one of Central Otago's finest dining experiences with exceptional wine. A true farewell splurge (~NZD 65-85 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Hill Time Walk starts from the end of Regent Street — allow 3 hours and bring water. The view from the summit 'Basket of Dreams' sculpture is iconic. If time allows, visit the Queenstown i-SITE to return any borrowed gear or maps. Pack carefully tonight — departure day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk to the lakefront — watch the Remarkables turn pink in the morning light. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast. Complete packing and check out of Nevis Valley Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either head directly to Queenstown Airport (~30 min from the Nevis Valley area) or enjoy a final coffee and browse at the Queenstown Farmers Market (if Saturday) or town centre. Transfer to airport and check in for departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days — two bungy jumps, the Routeburn Great Walk, Mueller Hut, Milford Sound kayaking, and the incomparable landscapes of New Zealand's South Island.

meals.breakfast: Final New Zealand breakfast — Vudu Café for eggs benedict and a flat white, or hotel breakfast (~NZD 20-28)
meals.lunch: Airport café at Queenstown Airport — grab a final Kiwi pie and flat white before boarding (~NZD 15-20)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in and security at Queenstown Airport. The airport is small but can get busy. Declare any food items at customs. New Zealand has very strict biosecurity — ensure no fruit, seeds, or used hiking boots with soil are in carry-on luggage. Consider purchasing travel insurance claim forms if any activities were disrupted by weather.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is a must for thrill-seekers, offering breathtaking views of the Central Otago landscape before the ultimate freefall lasting approximately 8.5 seconds.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular Great Walks, a 32km trail through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Trek through ancient beech forests, alpine meadows, and past stunning glacial lakes with panoramic views of the Southern Alps. A multi-day hike best done over 2-3 days.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Equivalent: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Hike the challenging Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a 10km round trip gaining 1000m in elevation. Reward yourself with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Glacier, and turquoise glacial lakes. Overnight stays in the DOC hut are available for a truly immersive alpine experience.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy jump site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River in a scenic gorge setting. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is perfect for first-timers and includes the option to touch the water on your jump.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayaking adventure on the mirror-like waters of Milford Sound with a hike along the Milford foreshore track. Paddle beneath towering 1200-meter cliffs, spot fur seals and dolphins, and witness the majestic Stirling and Bowen Falls up close. A truly unforgettable Fiordland wilderness experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Settle into your luxury accommodation, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the property grounds to soak in the dramatic Nevis Valley landscape and alpine scenery
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at your boutique stay or a short drive to Queenstown's acclaimed Amisfield Winery & Bistro for a celebrated Central Otago wine dinner experience featuring seasonal tasting menus paired with estate pinot noir

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at Queenstown Airport lounge or a quick stop at Vudu Cafe & Larder in Queenstown town centre en route to the hotel
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — multi-course seasonal tasting menu with Central Otago wine pairings (book in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport in advance. The Nevis Valley road can be rugged — confirm vehicle access with your accommodation. Jet lag management: keep the first evening relaxed. Check-in time and any welcome amenities with the boutique stay ahead of arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump — experience the world's first commercial bungy jump site, leaping 43 metres above the turquoise Kawarau River. This iconic historic site is approximately 20 minutes from Queenstown and an unmissable adrenaline milestone. Book the VIP experience for exclusive viewing decks and a private debrief
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-bungy recovery and celebration: explore the Kawarau Bridge visitor centre and AJ Hackett facilities, then head into Queenstown for a leisurely stroll along the lakefront promenade. Browse Queenstown's premium boutiques or visit the Queenstown Gardens for a peaceful afternoon walk
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Rata Restaurant by Chef Josh Emett — one of Queenstown's finest dining establishments celebrating New Zealand produce in an elegant setting

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at your Nevis Valley boutique stay — expect fresh local produce, artisan breads, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: The Bunker Restaurant in Queenstown — a cosy, upscale hidden gem serving premium burgers, craft cocktails, and New Zealand craft beers
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant — seasonal New Zealand tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy VIP package well in advance. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. The jump is suitable for most fitness levels. Weather can affect jump operations — have a flexible backup plan. Bring a GoPro or purchase the professional video package on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — the crown jewel of New Zealand bungy jumping. Plunge 134 metres above the spectacular Nevis River gorge in a gondola-suspended pod. This is the Southern Hemisphere's highest bungy and an absolute bucket-list experience. The full VIP package includes private transfers in a 4WD, exclusive pod access, and professional media capture
day_by_day.afternoon: Nevis Valley exploration — after the adrenaline rush, take a guided 4WD heritage tour of the Nevis Valley, learning about its gold mining history and dramatic schist rock formations. Alternatively, enjoy a private picnic lunch in the valley arranged by your boutique stay
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a private chef dinner experience or in-room spa treatment. Many luxury boutique properties in the Nevis Valley can arrange private dining under the stars with unobstructed views of the Milky Way

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh Central Otago stone fruits, local honey, artisan pastries, and eggs from nearby farms
meals.lunch: Private luxury picnic in the Nevis Valley gorge — arranged by your accommodation with charcuterie, local cheeses, Central Otago pinot gris, and seasonal salads
meals.dinner: Private in-accommodation chef dinner — a curated 4-course New Zealand tasting menu with matched wines, served under the stars or in a private dining room

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a dedicated 4WD transfer — typically included in the VIP package. Minimum weight requirements apply (45kg). The experience takes approximately 3–4 hours including transfers. This is an ideal day to keep the afternoon relaxed given the physical and emotional intensity of the jump. Confirm all bookings at least 2 weeks prior.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle toward Glenorchy (approximately 45 minutes from Queenstown). Begin the Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 1 of a 2-day guided premium hiking experience. Hike from the Routeburn Shelter through ancient beech forest to the Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4 hours, 8.5km). Enjoy cascading waterfalls and alpine meadows along the way
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking above the bushline to the spectacular Routeburn Falls viewpoint. Take in panoramic views of the Humboldt Mountains and the lush Routeburn Valley below. Arrive at the premium Routeburn Falls Hut or a private guided lodge accommodation if booked
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Routeburn Falls area — if booked through a premium guided operator such as Ultimate Hikes, enjoy a private lodge experience with hot meals, wine, and comfortable bunks or private rooms

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — packed trail snacks and a premium trail lunch box prepared by the guided operator
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch provided by Ultimate Hikes guided service — typically includes wraps, fresh fruit, energy bars, and hot drinks at hut stops
meals.dinner: Hearty 3-course guided lodge dinner at Routeburn Falls Lodge — New Zealand lamb, seasonal vegetables, and dessert with wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the Routeburn Track through Ultimate Hikes for the fully guided premium experience including lodge accommodation, all meals, and expert guides. November is an excellent time — wildflowers bloom and snow may still cap the peaks. Pack layers, waterproof gear, and broken-in hiking boots. Luggage transfer service available so you only carry a daypack.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 2 — depart Routeburn Falls Lodge early and ascend to Harris Saddle (1,255m), the highest point of the track. On clear days, views stretch across to Fiordland and the Tasman Sea. This is among the most breathtaking alpine panoramas in the Southern Hemisphere
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the Hollyford Valley into Fiordland National Park, passing Lake Mackenzie and the dramatic Earland Falls (174m). Arrive at the Divide on the Milford Road for private vehicle pick-up. Transfer by luxury vehicle to Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland — approximately 1 hour
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a premium Te Anau property (recommend: Te Anau Lodge or Fiordland Lodge for luxury). Enjoy a relaxed evening with a long soak and a celebratory dinner after completing the Routeburn Track

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Routeburn Falls Lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Trail lunch provided by Ultimate Hikes at Lake Mackenzie Hut — soup, sandwiches, and hot drinks
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge Restaurant or The Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — celebrated for its wild venison, blue cod, and Fiordland-inspired cuisine with excellent New Zealand wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section can be exposed to wind and weather — dress in waterproof layers regardless of forecast. Total Day 2 hiking is approximately 11km. Arrange private transfer from The Divide to Te Anau in advance. Celebrate completing the Routeburn — it is one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks and a genuine achievement.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — depart Te Anau early by private vehicle along the iconic Milford Road (approximately 2 hours, stopping at Mirror Lakes and The Chasm along the way). Begin a guided sea kayaking adventure on the glassy waters of Milford Sound, paddling beneath Mitre Peak (1,692m) and beside towering waterfalls
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the combo experience with a guided hike along the Milford foreshore or a short section of the Milford Track. Spot New Zealand fur seals basking on rocks, Fiordland crested penguins, and dolphins playing in the sound. Return to the Milford Sound visitor area for a private cruise option or simply take in the scenery
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau along the Milford Road — stop to photograph the sunset over Lake Te Anau. Dinner at your Te Anau accommodation or at a local fine dining venue

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Te Anau lodge before departure — packed snacks for the Milford Road journey
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by your guided kayak operator — enjoyed on the water or at a scenic rest stop
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge or Te Anau Lodge private dining — wild blue cod, Fiordland venison, or seasonal New Zealand lamb with Central Otago pinot noir

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo through a premium operator such as Rosco's Milford Kayaks or Real Journeys. Depart Te Anau by 7:00am to maximise time on the water before afternoon tour groups arrive. November weather in Fiordland can be wet — Milford Sound receives over 7 metres of rain annually, which only adds to the dramatic waterfall spectacle. Waterproof gear provided by operator.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Te Anau. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Explore Te Anau township — visit the Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre for an introduction to the region's ecology, then walk the easy Lake Te Anau Walkway along the shore for spectacular views of the Murchison Mountains
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves private tour — take a boat across Lake Te Anau to the mysterious limestone caves filled with glowworms (Arachnocampa luminosa). Book a private or small-group guided tour for an intimate, premium experience. Alternatively, enjoy a private helicopter scenic flight over Fiordland and Doubtful Sound
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Te Anau dinner — indulge in a long, leisurely meal celebrating the Fiordland leg of your journey before preparing to head toward Mount Cook

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at your lodge — sleep in and enjoy at leisure
meals.lunch: Sandfly Cafe in Te Anau — beloved local favourite with excellent cabinet food, coffee, and lakefront views
meals.dinner: The Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — rustic fine dining in a heritage building with a celebrated menu of wild South Island game, seafood, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour is operated by Real Journeys — book the private experience for a more exclusive visit. The helicopter option over Fiordland is extraordinary on clear days — operators include Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters. This is a deliberate rest day after four consecutive days of intense activity. Use the afternoon to recharge, do laundry, and prepare gear for the Mount Cook section.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau by private luxury vehicle toward Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park — a scenic 4-hour drive via Lake Pukaki and the Mackenzie Basin. Stop at the Church of the Good Shepherd at Lake Tekapo for photographs of the iconic alpine chapel against the turquoise glacier-fed lake
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mount Cook Village and check in to The Hermitage Hotel — the iconic luxury lodge at the foot of Aoraki/Mount Cook. Take an introductory walk on the easy Kea Point Track (2 hours return) for stunning views of the Mueller Glacier and Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724m), New Zealand's highest peak
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at The Hermitage's The Panorama Restaurant — floor-to-ceiling windows frame Aoraki/Mount Cook as you dine on premium New Zealand cuisine. If skies are clear, join a guided Dark Sky stargazing session — the Mackenzie Basin is an International Dark Sky Reserve

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Te Anau lodge before departure or a packed gourmet breakfast box for the road
meals.lunch: Picnic stop at Lake Pukaki lookout — arrange a luxury hamper through your accommodation or stop at the Lake Pukaki Visitor Centre cafe
meals.dinner: The Panorama Restaurant at The Hermitage — celebrated for its views and refined New Zealand tasting menus with matched wines

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Te Anau to Mount Cook is approximately 4 hours without stops — allow 5–6 hours with scenic detours. The Lake Pukaki viewpoint is unmissable — the vivid turquoise colour comes from glacial flour suspended in the water. Book The Hermitage well in advance as it fills quickly in November (summer season). Confirm stargazing session availability on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Mueller Hut Route — begin the challenging and rewarding 10km round trip hike from White Horse Hill Campground, gaining approximately 1,000 metres of elevation. The trail ascends via the Sealy Tarns Track through alpine meadows and rocky terrain to Mueller Hut at 1,800 metres
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mueller Hut for breathtaking 360-degree views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Mueller and Hooker Glaciers, and the Southern Alps. Enjoy a packed lunch at the hut while taking in one of the most spectacular alpine panoramas in New Zealand. Begin descent in the early afternoon
day_by_day.evening: Return to The Hermitage for a well-earned hot shower and rest. Celebrate the hike with a premium dinner and a glass of Central Otago pinot noir. Optional: evening soak if spa facilities are available

meals.breakfast: Early full cooked breakfast at The Hermitage before the hike — fuel up with eggs, local smoked salmon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch packed by The Hermitage kitchen — enjoyed at Mueller Hut with Aoraki/Mount Cook as your backdrop
meals.dinner: The Hermitage — Al's Bar & Grill for a more relaxed post-hike dinner, or The Panorama Restaurant for a special celebration meal

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Hut Route is graded as demanding — expect 4–6 hours return. Start by 7:30am to avoid afternoon weather build-up. Wear sturdy hiking boots, carry waterproofs, and bring sunscreen and sunglasses (UV is intense at altitude in November). The upper section involves steep rocky scrambling — trekking poles recommended. Check DOC conditions report the evening before. This is one of the finest day hikes in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Hooker Valley Track — a beautiful, accessible 3-hour return walk along the Hooker Valley floor with iconic views of Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in Hooker Lake. Cross three swing bridges and walk alongside the retreating Hooker Glacier terminal lake with floating icebergs. A perfect active recovery hike after yesterday's demanding climb
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic helicopter flight over Aoraki/Mount Cook and the Southern Alps — book a premium 45-minute or 1-hour flight with a snow landing on the Tasman Glacier. Operators such as The Helicopter Line offer exclusive experiences with champagne on the glacier. This is an extraordinary and unmissable luxury highlight
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from The Hermitage terrace — Aoraki/Mount Cook turns golden pink at sunset in November. Farewell dinner at The Panorama Restaurant before preparing to head to Queenstown tomorrow

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at The Hermitage — enjoy the mountain views over coffee and a full cooked spread
meals.lunch: Old Mountaineers' Cafe in Mount Cook Village — a beloved climbers' institution serving excellent homemade soups, pies, and coffee in a cosy setting
meals.dinner: The Panorama Restaurant at The Hermitage — final night celebration dinner with a premium degustation menu and sommelier wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter glacier landing well in advance — these flights are extremely popular in November and weather-dependent. The Hooker Valley Track is suitable for all fitness levels and is one of New Zealand's most iconic short walks. Combine both activities for a perfect balance of accessible scenery and luxury adventure. Pack layers for the helicopter flight — glacier temperatures are significantly colder than the valley.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mount Cook by private vehicle toward Queenstown — approximately 3.5 to 4 hours via the Lindis Pass. Stop at Omarama for breakfast and a visit to the famous Clay Cliffs — dramatic eroded pinnacles of silt and gravel forming an otherworldly landscape just minutes from the highway
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Queenstown by midday. Check back into your Nevis Valley Boutique Stay or a Queenstown luxury property for the final nights. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy Queenstown's lakefront, browse the Saturday Queenstown Farmers Market (if timing aligns), or indulge in a premium spa treatment at a Queenstown day spa
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown fine dining — a celebratory dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro or Botswana Butchery on the Queenstown lakefront, celebrated for its premium New Zealand beef and lamb with spectacular lake and mountain views

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at The Hermitage before departure, or stop at Omarama's Wrinkly Rams Cafe for a country-style cooked breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic stop en route at Lake Benmore or a roadside cafe in the Mackenzie Basin — arrange a packed luxury hamper from The Hermitage
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — premium New Zealand beef, Central Otago lamb, and an extensive wine cellar in a stunning lakefront setting

day_by_day.notes: The Lindis Pass route is scenic but can be exposed to wind — drive carefully in a rental or private vehicle. The Clay Cliffs at Omarama require a small entry fee and are a 15-minute detour well worth making. Allow time for a spa afternoon in Queenstown — ONSEN Hot Pools is a premium Queenstown experience with private cedar hot tubs overlooking the Shotover River canyon.

day_by_day.morning: ONSEN Hot Pools private session — book a private cedar hot tub pod overlooking the Shotover River canyon for a deeply restorative morning. This is Queenstown's most luxurious relaxation experience and a perfect counterpoint to the week's physical adventures
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown gondola and luge — ride the Skyline Gondola to Bob's Peak for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Enjoy the premium Stratosfare Restaurant lunch with a view, then take a scenic walk along the Ben Lomond Track above the gondola for additional alpine views without the full summit commitment
day_by_day.evening: Final Queenstown dinner — reserve a table at Amisfield Winery & Bistro for a farewell feast celebrating 13 days of extraordinary South Island experiences. Alternatively, book a private winery dinner at Peregrine Wines in the Gibbston Valley for an intimate cellar door experience

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at your boutique stay — enjoy a slow, leisurely final full breakfast
meals.lunch: Stratosfare Restaurant at the Skyline Gondola — buffet-style premium lunch with panoramic 360-degree views of Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — trust the chef multi-course menu with full Central Otago wine pairing; one of New Zealand's finest dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Book ONSEN Hot Pools private pods in advance — they are extremely popular and often sold out weeks ahead in November. The Skyline Gondola experience includes the luge, which is surprisingly fun for adults. The Ben Lomond Track above the gondola offers a more adventurous alternative to the tourist areas — allow 1–2 hours for the lower section. This is your last full day — savour Queenstown at a relaxed pace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown — enjoy a slow farewell breakfast at your boutique stay. Take a final lakefront walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront or visit the Queenstown Memorial Centre. Pick up any last-minute New Zealand souvenirs — recommend Remarkable Sweet Life chocolates, local manuka honey, or Central Otago pinot noir to take home
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Enjoy the Queenstown Airport premium lounge if available with your airline or Priority Pass membership
day_by_day.evening: Departure — farewell to an extraordinary 13-day South Island adventure spanning world-class bungy jumps, Great Walk hiking, Fiordland sea kayaking, Mueller Hut alpine climbing, and Tasman Glacier helicopter landings

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — savour every bite with views of the Nevis Valley for the last time
meals.lunch: Queenstown Airport or a final quick lunch at Vudu Cafe & Larder in town before transfer — excellent coffee, cabinet food, and a relaxed atmosphere
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge — consider purchasing a bottle of Central Otago pinot noir at the airport duty-free to enjoy as a memory of the trip

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and airport transfer booking the evening before. Queenstown Airport is small but can be busy in November — arrive early. Pack any hiking gear, wet clothing, and souvenirs carefully. Reflect on an extraordinary itinerary: two world-class bungy jumps including the 134m Nevis, the Routeburn Great Walk, Milford Sound kayaking, Mueller Hut Route, and a Tasman Glacier helicopter landing — a genuinely premium and unforgettable South Island adventure.
